page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.sn2ne.6xlarge is a general-purpose instance featuring 24 vCPUs across 12 physical cores on an Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor running at 2.5 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture with dedicated CPU allocation, it includes hyperthreading with 2 threads per core, a 35 MB L3 cache, and instruction set extensions such as AVX, AVX-512, AES, FMA, and BMI2. The system provides 96.0 GB of RAM, maintaining a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. It includes no local storage, requiring network-attached storage for persistent data, and features a 4 Gbps baseline network bandwidth with no complimentary public IPv4 addresses or dedicated GPUs.

Benchmark analysis reveals a distinct contrast between single-core and multi-threaded throughput. Single-core performance falls in the bottom 25 percent across stress-ng (1108.29) and Geekbench (942.0), with single-threaded gzip compression registering in the bottom 10 percent (19.06 GB/sec). Conversely, multi-core utilization achieves middle 50 percent average results, evidenced by a multi-core stress-ng score of 17646.71, a PassMark CPU score of 18419.6, and a multi-threaded bzip3 decompression throughput of 83.04 GB/sec. Uncached memory read and write bandwidth measure 90.83 GB/sec and 53.0 GB/sec respectively, supporting average operational speeds in Redis SET requests at 16.93 million operations per second and database operations at 6441.03 operations per second.

Given its Intel Xeon E5 Broadwell hardware generation, the instance provides steady compute density and balanced resource distribution without high-frequency single-thread premium costs. The lack of local NVMe SSD storage and modest 4 Gbps baseline networking are key architectural tradeoffs. The ecs.sn2ne.6xlarge is best suited for horizontally scaled multi-threaded applications, general enterprise web serving, internal microservices, software compilation pipelines, and containerized caching tiers where individual core execution speed is secondary to aggregate multi-core volume.
